key_insight: Teleportation overhead in distributed quantum chemistry circuits varies strongly by ansatz and qubit mapping, with UpCCD under spin-blocked Jordan-Wigner giving the best scaling and UCCSD the worst.
engineering_relevance: For distributed quantum computers, ansatz and encoding choices directly determine Bell-pair and classical-communication costs, shaping whether chemistry workloads are practical across modular hardware.
method: Compared teleportation-based DQC resource costs for UCCSD, UpCCD, and UpCCGSD on hydrogen-chain problems.
Contrasted a naive distribution strategy with TeleSABRE-optimized placement/routing.
Evaluated nonlocal two-qubit gate costs under fixed midpoint and quarter-point partitions for Jordan-Wigner and Bravyi-Kitaev encodings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative estimates of Bell-pair and classical-communication overheads, showing consistent resource advantages for UpCCD with spin-blocked Jordan-Wigner over the other ansätze.
watch_item: The results are specific to teleportation-based distribution and the chosen hydrogen-chain partitions, so overheads may shift for different molecules, layouts, or DQC protocols.
paper_title: Quantifying Teleportation Overhead in Distributed Unitary Coupled-Cluster Ansätze
